topic: Conditional efficiency bound for staggered triple differences. In an iid fixed-T panel with adoption cohort G, eligibility S, covariates X, overlap, no anticipation, and the target-indexed covariate-conditional DDD parallel-gap restrictions of Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna, fix finitely many group-time ATTs and a prespecified aggregate omega. Use every admissible clean comparison cohort. Derive the full observed-law tangent space and canonical gradient. Prove, rather than assume, that the efficient gradient is the joint OVS score vector Psi weighted by b*(x)=Gamma(x)^(-1)A{A'Gamma(x)^(-1)A}^(-1)omega, with the correct operator form for singular fixed-rank cases. Construct an attaining cross-fitted estimator under explicit overlap, conditional-eigenvalue, L4, nuisance and learned-weight product-rate conditions, with pointwise Wald inference. Characterize exactly when OVS's published loading and the parent's best constant joint loading satisfy the pointwise projection equations. Give a bounded open binary-covariate family where conditional weighting strictly beats every constant loading, and pointwise inference for the efficiency gap away from equality. Integrate the method as an optional backend for CRAN triplediff; do not call score-class projection semiparametric efficiency before tangent exhaustion is proved. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived Var{b(X)'Psi}=Var{omega'h(X)}+E[b(X)'Gamma(X)b(X)] and its pointwise constrained optimizer, including the singular operator condition. A legal binary-X mixture of the parent's bounded witness with rho_x=xr makes every constant loading choose q=0 while q*(x)=xr omega_2/2; the exact gain is 3r^2 omega_2^2/32, equal to 3/512 at r=omega_2=1/2, with separated conditional eigenvalues. Current searches distinguish overidentified staggered DDD from just-identified DDD EIFs and efficient DiD. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove local full-data-to-observed equivalence and tangent exhaustion: every regular aggregate gradient must differ from a fixed pairwise gradient exactly by the closure of measurable conditional clean-comparison contrasts. Without this theorem, b*(X)'Psi is only optimal in a chosen score family. Then control shared-cell covariance and learned-weight remainders. EARLY KILL TEST: Symbolically differentiate the finite-support binary-X three-score submodel under both conditional clean-cohort equalities, compute its complete tangent matrix, and verify that the projected gradient is b*(X)'Psi with gain 3/512. Any extra variance-reducing direction, missing gradient, or omitted compatibility restriction kills the canonical-gradient claim. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_staggered_ddd_conditional_efficiency_bound.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: OVS establish only unconditional GMM optimality for their retained staggered-DDD scores. The banked parent likewise proves optimality only in a finite constant score span, while its rejected angle asserted—but did not prove—the tangent-space equality. Chen–Sant'Anna–Xie prove the analogous exhaustion step for staggered DiD, but eligibility introduces additional conditional equalities, target-share derivatives, and compatibility across cohorts sharing outcome histories. What remains missing is an integrability argument showing that every observed-law score satisfying the linearized DDD restrictions arises from a regular submodel and that no additional observed restriction supplies another variance-reducing direction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observed-law equivalence and exact closed-tangent-space theorem, followed by a projection and convolution theorem identifying b*(X)'Psi as the unique canonical gradient and its variance as the semiparametric efficiency bound.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Both banked DDD angles impose invertibility exactly where shared or redundant clean comparisons can make Gamma(x) singular. Newey supplies abstract generalized-inverse machinery, and the PT/SC proposal handles finitely redundant normal rows, but neither establishes the measurable range geometry of the conditional DDD operator. The missing first step is to characterize range and null spaces almost surely, prove compatibility of A'b=omega, show that ker Gamma changes do not alter the L2 gradient, and control measurability of the pseudoinverse. Rank variation or an incompatible aggregate can otherwise destroy existence or uniqueness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fixed-rank operator theorem giving necessary and sufficient feasibility conditions, an explicit Moore–Penrose canonical-gradient formula in the L2 quotient, and counterexamples showing failure under each omitted compatibility condition.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The completed parent learns only an unconditional finite-dimensional covariance and constant loading. Once b*(x) depends on an estimated Gamma(x), its error multiplies a score vector whose coordinates reuse outcome cells; generic DML arguments do not automatically control that shared-cell remainder. The rejected angle omitted the empirical-process, covariance-learning, inversion, ridge, and product-rate inequalities needed to show that weight estimation is second order and that the plug-in variance estimates the canonical-gradient variance. Existing papers provide basic DDD cross-fitting or learned optimal instruments separately, but not this combined staggered-DDD result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified cross-fitted estimator with an asymptotic-linear expansion in b*(X)'Psi, a consistent influence-function variance estimator, explicit L4 and nuisance-by-weight product-rate conditions, and a pointwise studentized N(0,1) limit.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent classifies only unconditional separate-versus-joint constant loadings through a finite covariance equation and leaves the labelled-incidence classification open. OVS do not characterize when their loading also solves the conditional problem, while the DiD efficiency literature shows that pointwise weights are generally different. A valid DDD classification must combine the conditional affine projection equations with covariance maps realizable by shared bounded panel histories; an abstract positive-definite matrix is not enough. Inference adds a nonlinear optimized-value functional whose derivative includes learned covariance and loading terms, and ordinary Wald theory degenerates on the equality frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if pointwise projection classification for both constant-loading architectures, a bounded compatible binary-X family with a closed-form positive gain on an open parameter region, and an influence-function CLT with a consistent Wald interval for the gain on laws separated from equality.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing results cover separate corners: basic repeated-cross-section DDD, overidentified staggered DDD in balanced panels, and efficient repeated-cross-section DiD under compositional change. In the combined setting, within-unit outcome differences are unavailable or partially missing, sampling-time and observation-pattern scores enlarge the tangent space, and covariance between clean comparisons comes from shared sampled cells rather than complete trajectories. The literature scan found no observed-law characterization or conditional all-cohort efficiency result for that joint regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observed-data identification and tangent-space theorem for staggered repeated-cross-section or unbalanced-panel DDD, an explicit conditional-covariance canonical gradient for a prescribed aggregate, and a cross-fitted attaining estimator with a pointwise CLT.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames why repeated-cross-section DDD is useful and why compositional change must be modeled.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: DDD uses an auxiliary eligibility dimension to relax ordinary parallel trends -> repeated cross-sections introduce changing composition and missing joint outcomes -> efficiently combine all valid staggered clean cohorts under that sampling regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct cross-fitted influence-function estimators for repeated-cross-section DDD and prove root-n normality and efficiency in the basic design.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the destination-regime DDD score and sampling terms that must be lifted into the staggered overidentified system.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the observed-data EIF under compositional change using generalized propensity scores for treatment-by-sampling-time cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those sampling and composition tangent components distinguish the destination from the fixed-panel model.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate all valid staggered comparisons and obtain the efficient conditional-covariance projection after proving observational equivalence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination combines this all-comparison machinery with the repeated-cross-section DDD influence structure.

literature_map:
Olden–Møen (2022, Econometrics Journal, doi:10.1093/ectj/utac010) formalize canonical DDD and show that one parallel trend in the difference of biases is sufficient.
Ortiz-Villavicencio–Sant'Anna (2025, arXiv:2505.09942) show failures of common covariate-adjusted and pooled staggered DDD procedures, construct clean-cohort DR scores, and combine them by unconditional GMM.
Their appendix derives an EIF only for a simple two-period DDD design; overidentified efficiency, adaptive nuisances, unbalanced panels, and repeated cross-sections remain open.
Akbari–Kiyavash–Ghassami (2025, arXiv:2502.19788) give semiparametric DDD identification and cross-fitted DR estimators for basic panel and repeated-cross-section designs, not the all-clean-cohort staggered system.
Sant'Anna–Zhao (2020, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.06.003) supply foundational doubly robust DiD scores and the two-period efficiency benchmark reused by later DDD work.
Callaway–Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1803.09015) establish conditional group-time ATT identification and inference under staggered adoption.
Chen–Sant'Anna–Xie (2025, arXiv:2506.17729) prove observational equivalence for overidentified staggered DiD and derive EIFs using covariate-specific covariance weights over all valid baselines and cohorts.
Chen–Xie (2026, arXiv:2510.16683) emphasize that efficiency in overidentified causal models requires first characterizing the induced observable statistical model.
Chamberlain (1987, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/0304-4076(87)90015-7) is the foundational optimal-instrument and efficiency-bound result for conditional moments.
Ai–Chen (2012, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2012.05.015) extend efficiency theory to sequential conditional moments containing unknown functions.
Newey (2001, Econometric Theory, doi:10.1017/S0266466601175018) treats singular conditional covariance through consistent linear systems and generalized inverses.
Ackerberg–Chen–Hahn–Liao (2014, Review of Economic Studies, doi:10.1093/restud/rdu011) prove efficiency for semiparametric two-step GMM with learned optimal weights and overlapping restrictions.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) provide the orthogonality, cross-fitting, product-rate, and Wald-inference template for learned nuisances.
Belloni–Chen–Chernozhukov–Hansen (2012, Econometrica, arXiv:1010.4345) show how optimal conditional instruments can be learned while preserving root-n inference.
Sant'Anna–Xu (2026, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2304.13925) derive efficient repeated-cross-section DiD under compositional change and a Hausman-type comparison test.
prior_proposal_map:
The active qid stat_staggered_ddd_conditional_efficiency_bound contains only run state, so no same-run proposal was available to mine.
The dominant source was the banked parent stat_ddd_overid_efficiency_v1, especially its README, final proto_core.json, and complete rejected efficiency angle proto_core_angle0_rejected.json.
All available parent proposal reviews were inspected: angle0 versions 1 and 4–11, angle1 versions 1–6, and final general, mathematical, and rubric reviews.
The highest-yield fields were angle1_v6.strengthening_paths, requesting the full EIF, an open strict-gain family, and gap inference, and angle0_v11.strengthening_paths, requesting explicit learner-rate and attainment conditions.
The rejected angle supplied unresolved theorem-level targets for tangent exhaustion, canonical-gradient derivation, conditional-weight cross-fit attainment, and shared-cell covariance projection.
The final parent README and reviews confirm that only constant-score-span optimality was completed and that full conditional-moment efficiency and gap inference remained outside scope.
Adjacent panel_ptsc_union_efficiency_envelope_v1 supplied a reusable tangent-normal and Moore–Penrose fixed-rank construction whose first DDD adaptation step is profiling eligibility-by-cohort restrictions.
No legacy DDD proposal TeX archive was needed because the closest parent uses the current proto_core and review layout.
